label: TMUA 2023 · Paper 2 · Question 18

hints.title: Use x squared as the variable
hints.body: Put u=x2. For a possible root u, consider how many real values of x it gives when u is positive, zero or negative.
hints.recap: A substitution must keep the restrictions on the new variable.
hints.pitfall: Two real u-values need not give four real x-values.
hints.pause: Write the quadratic in u and decide what its roots must be like.

recall.reminder: A substitution must keep the restrictions on the new variable.

hints.title: Check the smaller quadratic root
hints.body: Use the quadratic formula for u. Require different real roots, then require the smaller one to be positive.
hints.recap: If the smaller root is positive, the larger root is positive too.
hints.pitfall: Before squaring an inequality, check the signs of both sides.
hints.pause: Simplify the resulting conditions and match their combined range to an option.

recall.reminder: If the smaller root is positive, the larger root is positive too.

solution:
Put u=x2. Then u2+bu+c=0. To get four different real values of x, this quadratic must have two different positive roots.

The roots are u=−b±b2−4c2, so first require b2−4c>0. The smaller root is positive exactly when −b>b2−4c.

This requires b<0. Both sides are then nonnegative, so squaring gives b2>b2−4c, or c>0.

Combining b<0, c>0 and b2>4c gives c>0 and b<−2c. Conversely, these conditions give two distinct positive values of u, each producing two real values of x.

Answer D.
knowledgePattern: Translate four distinct quartic roots into two distinct positive quadratic roots
